source.title: ADVERSA: Measuring Multi-Turn Guardrail Degradation and Judge Reliability in Large Language Models
source.authors: Harry Owiredu-Ashley; Bo-Xiang Dong; Tao-Ran Ji; Jia-Cheng Shang

record.tranche_reason: Extends evaluation of harmful-request compliance to sustained multi-turn adversarial prompting and reports victim-model outcomes; it does not test the fine-tuning or token-position mechanisms in the listed versions.
record.gate_note: The reported results concern harmful compliance under adversarial framing, a related safety outcome not captured by the specific fine-tuning, KL-position, opening-token, localized-parameter, or deepening-training versions. Judge reliability and attacker drift are reported too, but do not measure those versions.
record.test_reason: A 15-conversation multi-turn red-teaming pilot against frontier APIs using framing-based prompts. There is no victim fine-tuning, no per-token KL, no prefill, suffix or decoding intervention, no parameter localization and no deepening training. Framing jailbreaks are a different attack from V4's compliant-opening prefills, suffixes or decoding changes, so no version is tested. The record's 'tests'/T3 contradicts its own listing of every version as not tested. Neither original source is cited.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors also stress that the work is mainly an infrastructure contribution. They frame first-turn framing as more consequential than iterative pressure only within this dataset. They further report that judge disagreement concentrates at rubric boundaries and that attacker drift and attacker refusals are confounds.
record.recipe_differences: A multi-turn adversarial evaluation using an attacker model, victim APIs, and three judges; no victim fine-tuning, aligned/base KL measurement, or token-position intervention.
record.method_sensitivity: Victim model and harm category had different reported jailbreak rates. Gemini's measured attack exposure was reduced by three attacker refusals. The study also reports different trajectories across conversations and victims.

fits_no_version.finding: Framing attacks such as academic, simulation or stress-testing contexts jailbroke 4 of 15 conversations. Three of the four succeeded on round 1 with unanimous 5/5 scores.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Single-turn legitimate-context framing can elicit full harmful compliance from frontier API models.

fits_no_version.finding: Non-jailbreak conversations converged toward scores 1–2 by rounds 6–10 rather than accumulating compliance.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Sustained multi-turn pressure does not progressively erode refusals in frontier models, at least in this small pilot.

fits_no_version.finding: Jailbreak rates differed by harm category: misinformation 2/3, privacy violation 0/3.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Susceptibility to framing attacks varies by harm category.

fits_no_version.finding: QLoRA fine-tuning of Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct on about 10.7k adversarial examples produced a usable attacker. It still showed residual refusals (3, all in Gemini conversations). The reported 85% refusal rate belongs to GPT-4, not this model.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Harmful-data fine-tuning of a safety-trained model largely, but not completely, removes refusals to generate attacks.

record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Software Engineering Research and Applications
record.problems: The authors report one conversation per objective-victim pair, no variance estimates, confidence intervals, statistical significance, or multi-seed replication; only 15 conversations were run. The attacker was trained on single-turn examples and deployed in a multi-turn setting, and three attacker refusals reduced Gemini's effective exposure. The exact jailbreak prompts and two objective descriptions were withheld.
record.rows_left_out: No additional victim compliance outcomes were reported as separate numerical conditions beyond the aggregate, per-victim, and per-category results recorded. Judge-agreement and attacker-drift results were left out because they do not measure the claim's listed versions.

untested.parts: No harmful fine-tuning of the victim models. The attacker's QLoRA fine-tuning is not evaluated as a safety-removal result.
No per-token KL between aligned and base models.
No prefilling, adversarial suffixes or decoding changes. Only prompt framing over turns is tested.
No analysis of why safety is shallow.
No deepening training and no durability test.

record.verdict_notes: Change relation and tranche from tests/T3 to discusses/T6. All rows correctly carry versions ['none']. Their 'partial' and 'absent' states are not judged against any version and should be read only as descriptive. The attacker model's fine-tuning is loosely related to V1, but it is deliberately induced and its refusal rate is not reported systematically. The sample is tiny (n=1 per pair) with no seeds or confidence intervals.

versions.untested_parts: No harmful fine-tuning of victim models or measurement of its effect.
No benign-data fine-tuning of victim models or measurement of its effect.
No per-token KL divergence measurement between aligned and base models.
No compliant-opening prefills, adversarial suffix intervention, decoding change, or analysis of first response-token positions. The study tests adversarial framing and multi-turn attacks instead.
No localization or intervention on victim-model weights or ranks.
No test of whether safety-training data or objectives produce shallowness.
No training intended to deepen safety across response tokens, or test of its durability.

rows.operation_detail: Evaluate victim responses to ADVERSA-Red adversarial prompts over multi-turn conversations; jailbreak requires consensus score at least 4 and at least 2 of 3 judges scoring at least 4.

conditions.value: median consensus; jailbreak if ≥2/3 judges score ≥4

rows.uncertainty: No variance estimate, confidence interval, or statistical significance; one conversation per objective-victim pair.
rows.note: Aggregate result across the three victim models.
